entries.title: Kobo Libra Colour will be on sale for Black Friday
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo has announced a sale on the Kobo Libra Colour, offering $30 off. It will be available on the Kobo website and through its retail partners. The sale runs from Nov 20th, 2026 to Dec 2nd, 2026. The post Kobo Libra Colour will be on sale for Black Friday first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Rakuten Kobo has announced a sale on the Kobo Libra Colour, offering $30 off. It will be available on the Kobo website and through its retail partners. The sale runs from Nov 20th, 2026 to Dec 2nd, 2026.

The Kobo Libra Colour is a standout, versatile e-reader for readers who want color-coded annotations, graphic novels, and seamless library access, though its screen comes with a trade-off for pure text purists. Its 7-inch E Ink Kaleido 3 display renders 300 PPI for black-and-white text and 150 PPI for 4,096 pastel-like colors, making book covers, comics, and multi-colored highlights genuinely enjoyable without the eye strain of a tablet. However, as reviewers at Six Colors point out, the color filter layer creates a slightly darker, textured background with lower contrast than traditional monochrome e-readers, meaning you will likely keep the ComfortLight PRO front light turned up higher during daily use.

Beyond the screen, the hardware design and software ecosystem are major highlights. Weighing around 200 grams with an ergonomic asymmetric grip, physical page-turn buttons, and IPX8 waterproofing, it is exceptionally comfortable for long, one-handed reading sessions. It also includes 32 GB of storage, weeks of battery life, built-in OverDrive/Libby integration for borrowing public library books, and Google Drive and Dropbox support for easy wireless file transfers. If you pair it with the optional Kobo Stylus 2 (sold separately), it doubles as a capable digital notebook for margin markups, though the lack of palm rejection requires tweaking touch settings to avoid accidental page turns while writing.

entries.title: E INK Announces E INK Spectra 6 with new colors
entries.summary: In 2026, E Ink Spectra 6 expanded from a 6-pigment architecture to a new "9-color system" and entered widespread adoption across consumer digital photo frames, large-format art posters, and DIY hardware panels. The post E INK Announces E INK Spectra 6 with new colors first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E INK has just announced a major upgrade to its Spectra 6 e-paper technology. It now supports 9 colors instead of 6. This increased range moves e-paper further beyond flatter, muted tones to render more vivid, natural-looking photographs. Audiences can experience 9-color up close in the new Ink 10″ from Aura, a cordless e-paper frame that brings photos to life with E Ink’s paper-like, low-power technology.

E Ink’s Spectra 6 9-color introduces orange, cyan, and light green to the existing palette of black, white, red, yellow, blue, and green. This expanded color range enhances color transitions, leading to smoother images with reduced pixelation. Achieving this level of complexity necessitates a robust driving system, requiring the 9-color display to be supported by a system-on-chip, along with an E Ink timing controller. For the foreseeable future, the 9-color display module will only be available in 10-inch sizes.

E Ink launched Spectra 6 as a full-color e-paper platform aimed at in-store advertising, indoor signage, home decor, and other applications that replace traditional paper signage. Its reflective display offers vibrant color for printed signage, while its low-power operation enables timely content updates with minimized energy consumption. The Spectra 6 9-color further advances this platform by providing a wider range of base colors for more intricate image reproduction.

“When Spectra 6 first launched a few years ago, it established a new color standard in e-paper – color that rivals the most advanced color paper printers on the market,” said JM Hung, president of E Ink Holdings. “Expanding six to nine base colors allows us to push that standard further and continue to make ePaper an appealing alternative to paper.”

The color possibilities of Spectra 6 9-color are showcased in Aura’s Ink 10″, the newest ePaper digital frame in the company’s Ink series. In contrast to conventional LCD photo frames with backlit displays, ePaper options like the Ink 10″ emulate the beauty and depth of printed photography without requiring power cords or continuous power sources. The combination of E Ink Spectra 6 9-color and Aura’s proprietary dithering algorithm enhances photographs with more uniform tones on faces, greater detail in textures, and smoother transitions in gradients. This cord-free, rechargeable frame is equipped with a 200 PPI display, an upgrade from the 150 PPI of the Ink 13″, allowing for sharper photo details that can last up to three months on a single charge. Its compact design is intended to suit various spaces, including desks, shelves, side tables, and gallery walls.

entries.title: CloudLibrary is available on all new Kobo e-readers
entries.summary: With the new partnership with OCLC’s CloudLibrary, Kobo is making it easier for readers to connect their favorite library catalogs to their eReaders, ensuring that no matter where you borrow your eBooks, they are ready and waiting on your device. The post CloudLibrary is available on all new Kobo e-readers first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
CloudLibrary is a service that lets you borrow eBooks and content from your public library. The service is quite popular among larger libraries that use OverDrive Libby; however, smaller branches may work only with CloudLibrary. CloudLibrary is supported on Kobo e-Readers running Kobo software version 4.38 or later. Kobo Clara BW, Clara Colour, and Libra Colour require version 4.46 or later.

“These days, the books readers love are coming from everywhere—from the Kobo Store and Kobo Plus of course, but also libraries, big publishers, indie bookstores, and beyond. We’ve realized that the more you read, the more likely it is that you want all your reading in one place. We want Kobo to be the home base for all of it,” said Michael Tamblyn, CEO of Rakuten Kobo. “Our goal is to make sure that whether you’re browsing on Kobo.com or borrowing from a library, the experience is the same: simple, quiet, and focused entirely on the book. By working closely with Libby and now, excitingly, CloudLibrary, we’re making sure that no matter where you find your next great story, it belongs on your Kobo.”

“We’re thrilled to bring CloudLibrary to Kobo, expanding access to thousands more library users,” said Drew Bordas, Chief Operations Officer, OCLC. “If your library has CloudLibrary, now you can discover and borrow eBooks easily in the CloudLibrary app, then enjoy a seamless, reader-first experience on your Kobo. We can’t wait for more readers to experience our collection on their Kobo.”

This update builds on Kobo’s existing, beloved Libby integration, which remains a cornerstone of the Kobo reading experience. Together, these partnerships ensure that Kobo readers have the most comprehensive, easy-to-use library borrowing experience available. CloudLibrary integration on Kobo E-Readers is currently available only for users whose library is located in the United States or Canada. Customers outside these regions will not see CloudLibrary as an available library integration option.

Connect your Kobo account to CloudLibrary

  • Open the CloudLibrary app or website and sign in.
  • Go to the Account tab.
  • Select Kobo Connect.
  • Tap or click Connect.
  • Sign in with your Kobo account email and password (or create an account if needed).
  • Follow the prompts to finish setup.
  • Once complete, you will see a confirmation that your Kobo account is connected.

Borrow books from CloudLibrary

CloudLibrary lets you send borrowed eBooks directly to your Kobo eReader. Here is how:

  • Sign in to your library.
    • Go to CloudLibrary or open the app.
    • Select your country, library, and enter your library card number and PIN.
  • Browse or search: explore featured titles or use the search bar to find books by title, author, or subject.
  • Borrow a book.
    • Select a title to see details and availability.
    • Tap Borrow to check it out instantly, or Place a Hold if it is unavailable.
  • Send to Kobo.
    • If the title is supported, you will see a “Send to Kobo” button.
    • Tap it to send the book to your Kobo account.
  • Sync your Kobo device.
    • On your Kobo eReader, tap Sync.
    • The book will appear in your library.
  • Read on Kobo: open the book directly on your Kobo and start reading or lis

entries.title: First Look at the Onyx Boox Note Air 6c
entries.summary: The Onyx Boox Note Air6 C is a 10.3-inch color E-Ink digital notebook and Android tablet running Android 16. The post First Look at the Onyx Boox Note Air 6c first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Onyx Boox Note Air 6C is their latest-generation tablet, released last month. It runs Google Android 16 and offers full access to the Google Play Store.

The display features a next-generation Kaleido 3 color screen protected by an anti-glare flat cover lens and illuminated by a dual-tone adjustable front light. It delivers crisp 300 ppi clarity for black-and-white content and 150 ppi for 4,096 vibrant colors. Page transitions and scrolling are driven by BOOX Super Refresh (BSR) technology, which increases page-turn speeds by 40% to 45% and heavily reduces visual ghosting compared to previous models

The BOOX Note Air6 C is a 10.3-inch color E Ink tablet powered by an upgraded 4nm octa-core processor, 6GB RAM, and 64GB of internal storage (expandable up to 2TB via microSD). Running Android 16 with full Google Play Store access, it features a tablet-style UI complete with customizable widgets and a dedicated app dock.

The ultra-thin 5.8mm premium aluminum chassis sports a unique purple-tinted black finish and houses a 3,700mAh battery alongside a fingerprint-enabled power button. The tablet integrates dual speakers and a magnetic pogo-pin connector that supports optional charging passthrough. It includes the new BOOX Pen3 Stylus, which offers 4,096 levels of pressure sensitivity for natural sketching and writing. The stylus features a unique, built-in replaceable-nib storage compartment hidden right inside the pen body for easy access on the go.

Despite its strong performance, the device carries the inherent trade-offs of Kaleido 3 color E Ink technology. The color layer makes the screen darker than black-and-white e-readers, requiring frequent use of the front light indoors, and colors appear muted with lower contrast compared to traditional tablets. Additionally, running full Android apps and fast refresh modes drains the 3,700 mAh battery quickly under heavy workloads, and its side-firing speakers sound thin. Overall, it is a top-tier choice for readers and note-takers who want full Google Play Store flexibility without eye strain, though existing Note Air5 C owners will find it an incremental upgrade.

Touch: BOOX stylus with magnetic type + capacitive touch. CPU: Qualcomm 6690 + BSR GPU. RAM: 6GB. ROM: 64GB. Connectivity: Wi-Fi + BT 6.0. Front Light with CTM (Warm and Cold)

entries.title: The Best Audible Audiobooks for November 2026
entries.summary: The best new Audible audiobooks for November 2026 feature major sci-fi audio dramas, returning fantasy favorites, gripping thrillers, and celebrity memoirs. The post The Best Audible Audiobooks for November 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The standout audiobooks across major platforms in November 2026 highlight blockbuster sci-fi sequels, cozy speculative fiction, dramatized adaptations, and Gothic horror.

Monsters of Ohio

Monsters of Ohio is a science fiction and dark humor novel by American author John Scalzi, published on November 3, 2026. Set in a struggling rural Midwestern town, the story blends body horror with social satire as residents suddenly begin transforming into bizarre monsters.

Peculiar Stars: A Novel

Peculiar Stars is a standalone contemporary romance novel by #1 New York Times bestselling author Rebecca Yarros, scheduled for release on November 17, 2026. Shifting away from the fantasy setting of her Empyrean series (Fourth Wing), the story follows a castaway romance centered on survival, self-discovery, and the aftermath of a public rescue.

Defy the Dusk: Book One of The Sundering Duet

Defy the Dusk is a post-apocalyptic fantasy romance novel by #1 New York Times bestselling author Danielle L. Jensen, published on November 3, 2026. It is the first installment in The Sundering Duet and blends gritty dystopian survival with a slow-burn, enemies-to-lovers romance.

A Parade of Horribles: Dungeon Crawler Carl, Book 8

A Parade of Horribles is the eighth novel in the bestselling Dungeon Crawler Carl LitRPG and sci-fi fantasy series by Matt Dinniman, published on May 12, 2026. Picking up amid the fallout of the Faction Wars, the story sends Carl and Princess Donut into high-stakes vehicular death races on the tenth floor of the World Dungeon.

All She Wants for Christmas: A simmering story of obsession

All She Wants for Christmas is a psychological thriller novella and Audible Original by #1 New York Times bestselling author Lisa Jewell, released on November 2, 2026. Designed specifically for audio with original music and sound design, this festive-set dark story explores marriage, jealousy, obsession, and the blurred line between truth and fiction.

Take My Word for It: A Memoir

Take My Word for It: A Memoir is a candid autobiography by actor, director, and literacy advocate LeVar Burton, co-written with Tracey Michae'l Lewis-Giggetts. Named after his signature Reading Rainbow catchphrase, the book reflects on his upbringing during the Civil Rights Movement, his breakthrough roles in Roots and Star Trek: The Next Generation, his personal mental health struggles, and his lifelong commitment to social equity.

Exoplanet

Exoplanet is a 7-episode science fiction audio drama written by Benjamin Percy and executive produced by Andy Weir (The Martian, Project Hail Mary), released exclusively on Audible on November 5, 2026. Blending hard sci-fi survival with a time-bending thriller, the story follows a scattered spaceship crew fighting to survive on an alien world across different eras.

The Telephone: A New History

The Telephone: A New History is a non-fiction history of technology book by bestselling science historian James Gleick, published on November 10, 2026. Marking 150 years since Alexander Graham Bell's first call, the book traces how the telephone evolved from an uncertain 19th-century novelty into the foundational network of the modern Information Age.

Warm Bodies

Warm Bodies is a dark psychological thriller novella by bestselling British author John Marrs, published on November 1, 2026 (with early access in October via Amazon First Reads). Released through Amazon Original Stories, this sharp, darkly comedic suspense tale follows an underestimated grandmother whose quiet village life hides a lethal secret.

A Court of Splintered Harmony

A Court of Splintered Harmony (subtitled The Valkyrie Cycle, Movement I) is the sixth novel in the #1 bestselling A Court of Thorns and Roses (ACOTAR) romantasy series by Sarah J. Maas, published on October 27, 2026. Serving as the opening movement of a new multi-part arc, the book expands the Maasverse with multiple perspectives as the Night Court faces a rising threat from Koschei the Deathless.

entries.title: Hunger Games, Owl Diaries available on Spotify Audiobooks
entries.summary: Spotify has partnered with Scholastic U.S. to bring the publisher's children's and family audiobook catalog directly to Audiobooks in Premium The post Hunger Games, Owl Diaries available on Spotify Audiobooks first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Spotify has partnered with Scholastic U.S. to bring the publisher’s children’s and family audiobook catalog directly to Audiobooks in Premium. Starting today, Premium subscribers in the U.S., U.K., Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Ireland can enjoy the Scholastic kids and family catalog, including titles previously available only for direct purchase, as part of their monthly audiobook listening allowance. That means series like The Hunger Games, Wings of Fire, Captain Underpants, and more are all just a tap away.

Suzanne Collins’s Sunrise on the Reaping was named Audiobook of the Year at the Audie Awards, and the film adaptation will be out this November. Hey, Kiddo, an immersive, full-cast audio adaptation of Jarrett J. Krosoczka’s graphic memoir is another favorite. For young readers, The Owl Diaries series by Rebecca Elliott, with principal narrator Emily Eiden, is a great full-cast production with music and sound design. Listeners also love what Zoe Boyle did with Billy Ray’s Burn the Water. Be sure to check it out before its sequel, The Water Will Fall, releases in March.

Since launching Audiobooks in Premium three years ago, Spotify’s collection has grown from 150,000 to 800,000 titles. And now, with new favorites from Scholastic US joining the mix, young readers have even more stories to discover.

“Scholastic is synonymous with childhood reading,” said Duncan Bruce, Director of Partnerships and Licensing at Spotify. “We’re thrilled to bring that catalog into Audiobooks in Premium, where families can discover and enjoy these titles freely within their monthly hours, helping to build lasting reading habits.”

entries.title: Craig and Marc Kielburger’s New Book With Martin Luther King III Says We’ve Been Chasing the Wrong Goal
entries.summary: Plenty of books promise to help you feel better. This one asks a harder question: what if the feeling was never the point? Grounded in Dr. King’s last sermon and backed by current research, Happiness vs. Fulfillment makes a persuasive case that the life most of us are after is not a happier one, but a more fulfilling one. The post Craig and Marc Kielburger’s New Book With Martin Luther King III Sa
entries.content:
Martin Luther King III, Arndrea Waters King, Marc Kielburger and Craig Kielburger have written a book for anyone who has ticked every box and still feels like something is missing.

Browse the self-help shelf on any e-reader store and you will find no shortage of promises to make you happier. There are more than 50,000 books about happiness on Amazon alone. A new release out this month takes the opposite position: the problem is not that we have not found the right path to happiness. It is that happiness was never the right goal.

Happiness vs. Fulfillment, published November 10, 2026, is co-written by civil rights leader Martin Luther King III, Drum Major Institute president Arndrea Waters King, and brothers Marc and Craig Kielburger. It runs 320 pages, carries a foreword by Mel Robbins, and grounds its argument in Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s final teachings and current research in neuroscience and psychology. Here is what is inside, and who it is for.

The big idea

The book draws a clear line between two states that most of us use as if they were the same.

Happiness, as the authors describe it, is a dopamine state. It runs on novelty, anticipation and the next reward, and it fades fast. Psychologists call the cycle the hedonic treadmill: no matter how much we achieve or buy, our emotional baseline resets and the search starts again.

Fulfillment is a serotonin state. It is built from gratitude, connection and meaning, and it does not depend on circumstances. The authors connect it to the ancient Greek idea of eudaemonia, which Aristotle described as the highest human good.

The book is careful not to frame this as a choice between fun and duty. “Fulfillment is not the opposite of happiness,” the authors write. “Fulfillment includes happiness. It’s just not dependent on it.”

The ‘Happiness Industrial Complex’

One of the more memorable sections takes aim at what the authors call the “Happiness Industrial Complex”: an economy of products, apps and quick fixes that profits from keeping people feeling that something is missing. The global wellness industry has grown to more than $6.8 trillion a year, they note, yet rates of anxiety and depression have kept climbing.

For readers who feel stuck, the book offers a line that is likely to be quoted often: “You are not broken. You are simply a human having a natural response to an unnatural system.”

How the book is built

Rather than a list of tips, the chapters are organized as a series of choices. A few examples:

  • Connection over disconnection. The authors argue that disconnection sits at the root of many modern crises, from loneliness to anxiety, and that reconnection is the antidote.
  • Now over past and future. Presence, they write, is what builds better futures, because good work, relationships and habits come from full engagement with today.
  • “We” over “me.” The final chapter makes the case that community is the foundation of both fulfillment and health.

The book describes the larger decision as “the choice that defines all other choices of how to live your life.”

It also has an unusual opening. The first pages return to February 1968, when Dr. King gave what became his final sermon to his home congregation at Ebenezer Baptist Church in Atlanta. Two months before his assassination, he told them he did not want to be remembered for his prizes or degrees, but for trying to love and serve others. The authors use that sermon as the thread that runs through the rest of the book.

Who wrote it

The four authors have worked together before. They co-host the award-winning My Legacy podcast and co-wrote What Is My Legacy?, which carried a foreword by the Dalai Lama. Happiness vs. Fulfillment picks up where that book left off.

Craig Kielburger is a New York Times bestselling author and social entrepreneur whose research looks at how purpose, contribution and legacy shape a fulfilling life. In 2026 he completed a doctorate in organizational development and change at Fielding Graduate University. His brother Marc Kielburger graduated from Harvard, studied law at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar and is a Member of the Order of Canada. The brothers co-lead Legacy+, and Craig serves as Chancellor of Legacy College.

Martin Luther King III is a civil rights leader and the eldest son of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and Coretta Scott King. Arndrea Waters King is president of the Drum Major Institute.

What early readers are saying

The book arrives with endorsements from some well-known names in the genre. Simon Sinek calls it “one of the essential maps to guide us on our journey.” Former U.S. Surgeon General Vivek Murthy writes that “its message could not be more important or timely.” In her foreword, Mel Robbins tells readers: “You’re about to learn a powerful way of living. A way of finding what truly matters and adding more of it into your life.”

Who should read it

Happiness vs. Fulfillment is a good pick if you:

  • Enjoyed Simon Sinek’s Start with Why or Mel Robbins’ work and want something that goes a step further, from motivation into meaning.
  • Are at a crossroads, such as a career change, retirement or a new chapter, and want a framework for what to build next.
  • Read a lot of popular psychology and want a book that ties the research to a moral tradition rather than a productivity system.
  • Teach or lead others. The publisher lists teachers, students and business readers as its core audiences, and the choice-by-choice structure works well for discussion groups and book clubs.

It is less suited to readers looking for a quick list of life hacks. The book asks you to rethink the goal itself, and it takes its time doing that.

The bottom line

Plenty of books promise to help you feel better. This one asks a harder question: what if the feeling was never the point? Grounded in Dr. King’s last sermon and backed by current research, Happiness vs. Fulfillment makes a persuasive case that the life most of us are after is not a happier one, but a more fulfilling one.

Book details – Title: Happiness vs. Fulfillment – Authors: Martin Luther King III, Arndrea Waters King, Marc Kielburger, Craig Kielburger – Foreword: Mel Robbins – Length: 320 pages – Published: November 10, 2026 – Where to buy: Amazon, Indigo and other major retailers

entries.title: Amazon Announces the Best Books of 2026
entries.summary: The Amazon Editors announced their Best Books of 2026, selecting American Hagwon by Min Jin Lee as their No. 1 pick – a sweeping family saga exploring ambition, sacrifice, and the enduring bonds between generations. The post Amazon Announces the Best Books of 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Today, the Amazon Editors announced their Best Books of 2026, selecting American Hagwon by Min Jin Lee as their No. 1 pick – a sweeping family saga exploring ambition, sacrifice, and the enduring bonds between generations. You can check out the full Best Books of the Year list at https://www.amazon.com/bestbooks.

The Best Books of 2026 list showcases the Editors’ top 20 overall picks, plus additional favorites across popular categories: Literature and Fiction, Mystery and Thrillers, Romance and Romantasy, History, Biographies and Memoirs, and Cookbooks. The list also introduces Buzzworthy, a new category for books people couldn’t stop talking about from this year and past years, and a Horror category for readers who love a good scare.

Sale American Hagwon

The National Book Award finalist and New York Times bestselling author of Pachinko returns with a breathtaking contemporary epic: a masterpiece by turns sweeping and intimate, that reckons with ambition and moderation, lust and loyalty, personal dreams and familial duty.

Exit Party: A Novel

The award-winning, bestselling author of Station Eleven and Sea of Tranquility returns with a breathtaking novel of doubles, shadow worlds, and fractured timelines as a man disappears from a glittering Los Angeles party, and a woman—a gunrunner, an art collector, an operative of the State—searches for answers.

Kin: Oprah's Book Club: A Novel

A magnificent new novel from the bestselling, award-winning author of An American Marriage—Tayari Jones has written an unforgettable novel that sparkles with wit and intelligence and deep feeling about two lifelong friends whose worlds converge after many years apart in the face of a devastating tragedy.

Sale Fruit Fly: A Novel

Fruit Fly: A Novel is a 2026 satirical thriller by Josh Silver. Published on August 4, 2026, this New York Times and USA Today bestseller blends dark comedy with psychological suspense to examine modern literary and identity culture.

entries.title: Adobe Acrobat will make editing PDFs in Gmail Google Drive easier
entries.summary: Google's partnership with Adobe will bring Adobe’s creative and productivity tools directly into the Google products you use every day. It will also bring Google’s frontier AI models into Adobe’s apps. The post Adobe Acrobat will make editing PDFs in Gmail Google Drive easier first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Adobe Acrobat is the best PDF viewer and editor, with tons of functionality. If you use Acrobat and Google products, there’s good news from the Adobe Max event. Adobe and Google have announced an expanded partnership that brings Adobe Acrobat directly into Gmail and Google Drive.

When previewing a PDF file in Google Drive or an attachment in Gmail, you will see a suggested “Edit with Acrobat” option. This creates a direct pathway to open, edit, and manage PDFs in Acrobat without needing to manually download the file first and upload it again. Adobe is expanding its connectors in Gemini and Gemini Enterprise with Acrobat and additional creative tools. Adobe will also bring its creative tools to AI Mode in Google Search. Adobe and Google DeepMind will explore new editing capabilities for creative professionals, starting with an image model for Photoshop that could enable near-real-time edits.

Businesses will be able to use Adobe’s CX Enterprise Coworker agent in Gemini Enterprise — an AI assistant that helps teams design graphics, work with PDFs, and launch marketing campaigns without switching apps.

The companies noted that these integrations are coming soon, though specific rollout dates, regional availability, and subscription or account requirements have not yet been fully detailed.

entries.title: Audible will provide audiobooks for underrepresented youth
entries.summary: Audible launched Imagine Louder, a global social impact initiative that provides free six-month Audible Premium memberships to 15,000 young people. The post Audible will provide audiobooks for underrepresented youth first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Audible has announced it will partner with non-profits with its Imagine Louder campaign. At launch, the program will provide free six-month Audible Premium memberships to 15,000 young people within its first three years, offering more than 180,000 hours of listening per membership. Audible will work with seven nonprofit organizations serving underrepresented youth aged 12 to 18 in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Mexico in the first year, with plans to expand to additional marketplaces in subsequent years.

The seven nonprofits selected for the first year of the program include Girl Rising in Mexico; DreamYard, Flockworks, and Life Anew Restorative Justice in the U.S.; and VICTA, Be Free Campaign, and Exodus Youth Worx UK in the UK, with plans to expand to more countries in following years.

Audible piloted the program for six months to help refine how it could best support young people. Early results showed the positive impact of audio storytelling paired with dedicated programming: 77 percent of caregivers in Audible’s U.S. pilot with the nonprofit Reading Partners rated their child “engaged” or “very engaged” with audio content, 100 percent of teachers in the National Literacy Trust’s UK pilot agreed the program encouraged students to listen to more audiobooks, and 95 percent of Girl Rising participants in Mexico agreed that stories are a tool for self-expression and personal development.

“Ages 12 to 18 are the years when young people are figuring out who they are and what’s possible for their lives, and the stories they hear can shape how they see themselves and the world around them,” said Aisha Glover, Global Head of Urban Innovation at Audible. “Imagine Louder puts the power of audio storytelling directly into the hands of young people who don’t always have the same access and opportunity and gives the organizations we work with the tools to make that experience their own.”

Tiffany Jackson, Head of Social Innovation at Audible, emphasizes, “We wanted to ensure that we weren’t just providing access alone. These organizations know best how to leverage audiobooks in a way that helps the young people they work with reach their full potential.”
